comments.text: Fence palings/sheets loose, damaged or leaning at [location]. Repair or replace affected sections.
Pool gate did not self-close and self-latch from all open positions at the time of inspection. Pool barrier compliance was not assessed.
Timber fence posts show decay at ground level, reducing stability.
Cracking to concrete path/driveway at [location], typical of shrinkage and minor ground movement. Monitor.
Displaced or uneven paving at [location] creates a trip hazard.
Retaining wall at [location] is leaning/bulging with cracking, indicating movement. Walls over 1 m may require engineering design and approval.
Timber sleepers to retaining wall show decay and deflection. Replacement will be required.
No visible drainage (weep holes or ag drain) to retaining wall. Hydrostatic pressure may cause future movement.
Ground surface falls toward the building at [location]; water is likely to pond against footings/slab edge.
Downpipe at [location] discharges onto the ground and is not connected to the stormwater system.
Surface drain/grated pit blocked with debris. Clear and test.
Steel posts to carport/shed corroded at the base. Treat or replace before section loss occurs.
Fibre cement sheeting to [location] may contain asbestos (age of material). Do not drill, cut or sand. Testing recommended before any work.
Large tree within close proximity of the building at [location]. Roots may affect footings, paths and drainage.
Vegetation overhanging the roof will deposit debris in gutters. Prune back.
Cracked, broken or displaced roof tiles at [location]. Replace to prevent water entry.
Corrosion to metal roof sheeting with perforation at [location]; water entry is likely. Replacement of affected sheets required.
Loose or missing roofing fixings at [location].
Pointing/bedding to ridge and hip capping cracked or deteriorated. Re-bed and re-point.
Flashing at [penetration/wall junction] is loose, lifted or poorly sealed.
Flashing at wall/roof junction is missing or inadequate, with evidence of water entry below.
Gutters contain debris and vegetation; overflow is likely in heavy rain. Clean and check falls.
Gutters/downpipes corroded or leaking at joints at [location].
Fascia/barge boards show decay and failed paint coatings at [location].
Eave lining sheets cracked, sagging or loose at [location].
Seals around roof penetration/skylight at [location] have deteriorated.
Hairline cracking (under 1 mm) to brickwork/render at [location], typical of minor movement. Monitor.
Stepped cracking to brickwork at [location], approx. [x] mm wide, indicating possible footing movement. Structural assessment recommended.
Weatherboards split, loose or decayed at [location], mainly to lower boards.
Window frames/sills weathered with decay at [location]. Paint coatings have failed.
Cracked glazing at [location].
Balustrade/handrail at [location] is loose, missing or below current height; openings may exceed 125 mm.
Stair stringers/treads at [location] are decayed or inadequately supported.
Deck posts/bearers decayed or inadequately supported and fixed (e.g. no stirrups, timber in ground) at [location].
Decking boards weathered, cupped or with loose fixings.
Signs of failed balcony waterproofing: staining/efflorescence to the soffit below.
Weep holes/subfloor vents obstructed by garden beds, paving or render at [location]. Clear obstructions.
Signs of rising damp to lower walls (efflorescence, mortar decay, high moisture readings) at [location].
External paint coatings weathered and flaking. Maintenance repainting required.
Cracking to ceiling sheet joints/cornice at [location].
Ceiling sagging at [location]; possible failed fixings. Risk of collapse. Avoid area until assessed.
Water staining to ceiling at [location] indicating a past or present roof leak. Moisture reading: [value].
Cracking above door/window head at [location], approx. [x] mm wide, typical of minor movement. Monitor; seek advice if it widens.
Wide or stepped cracking at [location] with doors binding, indicating structural movement.
Elevated moisture readings at base of wall adjoining wet area at [location].
Floor out of level with a noticeable fall at [location].
Springy or squeaking floor at [location]; framing or fixings may be inadequate.
Door at [location] binds on its frame or does not latch.
Window at [location] does not operate freely; hardware or locks broken/missing.
Base cabinet board under the sink is swollen from moisture. Check for leaks and replace damaged panel.
Benchtop joins/sealant deteriorated at [location].
Power outlet within close reach of the sink has a cracked cover.
Evidence of shower leak: elevated moisture, drummy/loose tiles and/or deteriorated grout, with staining to adjoining walls.
Silicone sealant around bath/shower/vanity has deteriorated. Remove and re-seal.
Inadequate exhaust ventilation; mould growth to ceiling.
Shower screen glass shows no visible safety glass marking.
Balustrade height and/or openings do not appear to meet current standards; horizontal elements may be climbable.
Smoke alarms missing, not interconnected or not in all required locations. Compliance with current requirements was not verified.
Damaged or exposed wiring/fittings observed at [location] (visual inspection only).
Roof framing members at [location] are cracked, sagging or inadequately supported/strutted.
Tie-down/bracing (straps, bolts) appears missing or inadequate at [location].
Insulation displaced or missing in areas, reducing thermal performance.
Sarking torn or sagging with signs of water entry at [location].
Ceiling battens/hangers detached at [location]; storage loads in roof void may be overloading the ceiling.
Downlights in contact with or covered by insulation; heat/fire risk.
Loose, unclipped cabling and/or junction boxes without covers in roof void.
Water staining to roof timbers/sarking at [location] indicating a roof leak.
Roof void access restricted at [location] by low clearance/insulation/ducting. Areas not inspected may conceal defects or timber pest activity.
Stumps/piers at [location] are leaning, settled or deteriorated (concrete spalling or timber decay).
Ant caps missing, damaged or not continuous at [location].
Bearers/joists at [location] are decayed, damaged or inadequately supported.
Packers loose or missing between stumps and bearers at [location].
Subfloor ventilation is inadequate; damp, musty conditions are conducive to timber pests and decay.
Ponding water/damp soil in the subfloor at [location].
Leaking or corroded pipework under the building at [location].
Timber debris/formwork left in the subfloor in contact with soil. Remove, as it attracts termites.
Active (live) subterranean termites found at [location]. Do not disturb. A treatment proposal and timber pest management program are strongly recommended.
Termite damage/workings found at [location]; full extent not determined. Invasive inspection and assessment of affected timbers recommended.
No durable notice or evidence of a current termite management system was sighted; treatment history unknown.
Evidence of borer activity (exit holes/frass) to [timber] at [location].
Fungal decay (wood rot) to [timber] at [location], typically from persistent moisture.
Conditions conducive to timber pest attack were noted. See the Conducive conditions section of this report.
Leaking tap/outdoor fitting at [location] is wetting the ground beside the building, which attracts termites.
Air-conditioner condensate and/or hot water relief overflow discharges against the building at [location]. Redirect away from the footings.
Elevated moisture readings at [location] (reading: [value]). Persistent moisture is attractive to termites and promotes fungal decay.
Leaking or overflowing gutters/downpipes are saturating the ground at [location].
Ground levels fall toward the building at [location], allowing water to pond against the footings/slab edge.
Downpipe at [location] discharges onto the ground beside the building and is not connected to stormwater.
Poor site drainage: damp or boggy ground beside the building at [location].
Garden bed/soil built up against the external wall at [location], covering the slab edge and weep holes. Concealed termite entry is possible.
Dense vegetation against the building at [location] restricts inspection and keeps the area damp.
Mulch or bark chip placed against the building at [location]. Keep mulch clear of walls and the slab edge.
Paving/concrete path laid against or over the slab edge at [location], bridging any termite barrier and concealing entry.
Timber posts/stumps embedded in or in contact with soil at [location].
Timber landscaping (sleepers, edging, retaining walls) in contact with the building or close to it at [location].
Timber debris, firewood or stored timber against the building or in the subfloor at [location]. Remove.
Timber stair stringers/lattice/cladding in contact with the ground at [location].
Subfloor ventilation is inadequate; damp, humid subfloor conditions are conducive to termites and fungal decay.
Subfloor vents blocked or obstructed at [location].
Enclosed areas beneath the building (storage, lattice, cladding) restrict airflow and inspection at [location].
Slab edge not visible for inspection at [location] (covered by soil, paving, render or cladding). Concealed termite entry is possible.
Weep holes covered or blocked at [location], concealing termite entry and trapping moisture.
Render/cladding extends to ground level at [location], bridging the slab edge.
No durable notice was sighted. Details of any termite management system and its maintenance history are unknown.
Durable notice sighted indicating treatment on [date]; the system may need inspection or renewal per the manufacturer’s requirements.
Ant caps missing, damaged or not continuous at [location].
Physical/chemical barrier appears breached or bridged at [location] (e.g. by new paving, garden beds or attached structures).
Tree stumps or old roots on the property at [location] may harbour termite colonies.
Large trees close to the building at [location] are a potential termite nest source. Consider a termite inspection of trees.
Timber fence attached to or in contact with the building at [location], providing a concealed termite pathway.
Timber deck/pergola/carport attached to the building with posts in ground at [location], bridging any barrier.
Extension or attached structure built after the original construction may not be protected by the termite management system.

Overall degree of risk of timber pest attack: [Low / Moderate / High], based on the conducive conditions noted and the property’s surroundings. More frequent inspections are recommended where risk is moderate or higher.
